claims.disproof_condition: Update if later G1 revisions or leg joints are shown to use different gearing (paper covers the arm only — leg actuators may differ, e.g., planetary for high-torque knees), or if a physical teardown names the harmonic-drive maker (would convert the supplier unknown into an edge).
claims.statement: Independent academic teardown-level evidence: every joint of the Unitree G1 arm (7 DOF, SDK indices 15-21) is a BLDC motor paired with a harmonic-drive reducer — resolving the reducer-scheme unknown from the G1 decompose with a third-party origin (Unitree's official specs do not disclose gearing). This ties the G1, a flagship low-cost humanoid, to the strain-wave-gear layer where HDS (sub=2), Leaderdrive and Shuanghuan already sit, and is consistent with the third-party report that Shuanghuan supplies Unitree — though WHICH maker's harmonic drives are inside the G1 remains unnamed in any primary source.

source_doc.title: Identification of a Physics-Based Electrical Power Consumption Model for the Unitree G1 Humanoid Arm (arXiv 2606.15915)

sources.quote: The Unitree G1 left arm has seven degrees of freedom: shoulder pitch/roll/yaw, elbow, and wrist roll/pitch/yaw (SDK motor indices 15–21). Each joint is driven by a BLDC motor paired with a harmonic-drive reducer.
Harmonic drives are not back-drivable; during deceleration the gear efficiency is ηg,i (not 1/ηg,i), making the model asymmetric.
